ports.readme:
# 📝 Living Code for Neovim **Calm slate. Living color.** Living Code for Neovim. Four color flavors, Tree-sitter and LSP highlights, and lualine integration. [Installation](#installation) · [Flavors](#flavors) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [All ports](https://github.com/living-code-theme) ## Previews
Night
Dark · full palette

 Frost
Dark · softer chroma
Paper
Light · near-white slate

 Signal
Dark · teal accent
Select any preview to view the image at full size. ## Installation Install with your plugin manager. For lazy.nvim: ```lua { "living-code-theme/nvim", priority = 1000, config = function() require("living-code").setup({ flavor = "night", transparent = false, italic_comments = true, }) vim.cmd.colorscheme("living-code") end, } ``` Or pick a flavor directly: `:colorscheme living-code-signal`. Covers Tree-sitter, LSP semantic tokens, diagnostics, gitsigns, telescope, nvim-cmp / blink.cmp, which-key, mini.*, lualine (`theme = "living-code"`). ## Flavors Expand a flavor for its full-size preview and activation instructions.
Night · Dark · full palette

Activate this flavor directly: ```vim :colorscheme living-code-night ``` Or set `flavor = "night"` in `require("living-code").setup()` before loading `living-code`.
Frost · Dark · softer chroma

Activate this flavor directly: ```vim :colorscheme living-code-frost ``` Or set `flavor = "frost"` in `require("living-code").setup()` before loading `living-code`.
Paper · Light · near-white slate

Activate this flavor directly: ```vim :colorscheme living-code-paper ``` Or set `flavor = "paper"` in `require("living-code").setup()` before loading `living-code`.
Signal · Dark · teal accent

Activate this flavor directly: ```vim :colorscheme living-code-signal ``` Or set `flavor = "signal"` in `require("living-code").setup()` before loading `living-code`.
## Configuration Call setup before loading the colorscheme. All options are optional: ```lua require("living-code").setup({ flavor = "night", light_flavor = "paper", transparent = false, italic_comments = true, dim_inactive = false, on_highlights = nil, }) vim.cmd.colorscheme("living-code") ``` With `background=light`, the default colorscheme selects `light_flavor`. A flavor-specific colorscheme always loads that flavor. For lualine, use `theme = "living-code"`. ## Compatibility Uses Neovim's Lua highlight API and true color. Includes Tree-sitter, LSP semantic tokens, diagnostics, gitsigns, telescope, nvim-cmp / blink.cmp, which-key, mini.* and lualine highlights. Plugin integrations are optional; install the plugins you use separately. ## Contributing Report installation issues and include the application version and selected flavor. For visual changes, include a real application screenshot. Keep this README, `port.json` and `images/` in sync; do not add generated mockups. 🦎 **One chameleon, many habitats.** Part of [Living Code](https://github.com/living-code-theme). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © Elliot Luque
